title: Scrambled Eggs
description: Scrambled Eggs are a breakfast classic made by gently cooking whisked eggs over low heat until soft, creamy, and delicately set. This professional chef's method creates rich, velvety curds with exceptional texture and flavor.

ingredients.title: Ingredients (serves 2)
items: 2 tbsp whole milk or heavy cream (optional, for extra creaminess)
Salt: pinch, preferably flaky sea salt
Fresh chives or parsley, finely chopped (for garnish)

instruction.title: 1. Prep the eggs
steps: Crack eggs into a bowl. Add milk/cream if using. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Whisk gently until yolks and whites are combined. Do not overbeat; you want a slightly streaky mixture for texture.

instruction.title: 2. Heat the pan
steps: Place the skillet over low to medium-low heat. Add butter and let it melt slowly. The butter should foam but not brown.

instruction.title: 3. Cook gently
steps: Pour the eggs into the pan. Let them sit undisturbed for a few seconds, then gently stir with a spatula, moving from the edges to the center.
Key: Low, slow cooking is essential for creamy texture. Avoid high heat; it will make the eggs rubbery.

instruction.title: 4. Create creamy curds
steps: Continuously but gently stir and fold the eggs. Stop cooking just before they’re fully set, as residual heat will finish them (carryover cooking).

instruction.title: 5. Finish
steps: Remove the pan from heat while the eggs are slightly runny. Give a final gentle stir. Taste and adjust salt/pepper if needed.

instruction.title: 6. Plating
steps: Serve immediately on a warm plate. Garnish with finely chopped chives or parsley.
For a continental flair, you can add:
A slice of toasted brioche or sourdough
Thinly sliced smoked salmon or prosciutto

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve immediately on a warm plate.
Garnish with finely chopped chives or parsley.
A slice of toasted brioche or sourdough.
Thinly sliced smoked salmon or prosciutto.

chefTips: Low and slow is the secret; never rush.
Use fresh, high-quality eggs for the best flavor and color.
Butter and cream make the texture luxurious; don’t skimp.
Serve immediately; scrambled eggs lose their texture quickly.
